lead.headline: Graf Zeppelin leaves Friedrichshafen for Lakehurst with 22 aboard
lead.deck: Berlin wire reports the ship away at 10:35 p.m. by New York time; Dr. Eckener in command; the Navy's seven stations to sit from Saturday; mast crew stood down until then
lead.body: The Graf Zeppelin left her shed at Friedrichshafen at 4:35 a.m. today, their time, or 10:35 p.m. yesterday by New York time, and set her course for Lakehurst, the Berlin wire states. Dr. Hugo Eckener is in command, with a crew of about 40 and 22 passengers. Her first message, received at the Naval Air Station at 11:58 p.m., read 'Lake Constance behind.' The Navy's seven receiving stations will sit from Saturday. The ground crew of 350 was stood down until then.

columns.headline: Arcade tenants to deposit the August rent of 412 dollars at 10 a.m. today
columns.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald states that the Vantry Arcade's ten tenants will deposit the August rent with the Municipal Court clerk at 10 a.m. today. The clerk will then hold 1,236 dollars for Signal Ground Rents Inc. Mr. Raab's papers remain visible in the company's post box.

columns.headline: Signal Exchange asks Mr. Crane for leave to lift the Ditmars Avenue seal
columns.body: The Queens Signal Exchange applied yesterday to Mr. Hollis Crane's office for leave to break the seal on the Ditmars Avenue room and lift its record since July 18, the Exchange states. Mr. Crane will rule under section 9. The owner of the house has not been found.

columns.headline: Stocks ease on 3,900,000 shares; ticker's tone entered as 'settling'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange eased yesterday on a volume of 3,900,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 358.7, a loss of 2.3. The ticker ran 8 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'settling.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 85. Thursday. The Zeppelin's up. The rent's in.

lead.headline: The Graf casts off for Lakehurst, and the Navy waits by the receiver
lead.deck: Dr. Eckener's first word home is about a lake; twenty-two passengers, forty crew, one ship the length of three city blocks, and the Speaker's office boy not among them
lead.body: Somewhere over Bavaria, at this moment, the Graf Zeppelin is coming our way with twenty-two passengers, forty crew and Dr. Eckener, who wired Lakehurst before midnight to say Lake Constance was behind him. So is most of Europe, by now. The Navy's seven listening stations start work on Saturday, and the three hundred and fifty sailors who catch the rope have the day off. Our office boy has the day off too. He spent it on the roof, listening east.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Will the Zeppelin ring ahead?'
columns.body: Madam, she rings the Navy, not you, and only when she has something to say, which so far is one lake. When she is near, the Montauk station will hear her engines. You will hear them too, if you live in Montauk. Otherwise, read the Speaker.

columns.headline: The Arcade's rent goes on deposit, and the company stays off the line
columns.body: This morning at ten the Arcade's ten tenants carry August's four hundred and twelve dollars to Mr. Ingersoll at the Municipal Court. That makes twelve hundred and thirty-six, held for a company with a post box and no voice. The pool says Friday.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week nine: the Zeppelin cards are cleared for landing
columns.body: The two hundred Zeppelin entries held since July go before the judges tomorrow with this week's six hundred. Horse puns remain disqualified. Mr. Kehoe's horse has submitted a card about a gasbag, which counsel says is not a horse pun. The judges are considering it.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Over Ulm at one this morning, says Berlin, making forty-five miles an hour into a head wind. Lakehurst says take your time.

lead.headline: Arcade tenants deposit the August rent; court clerk holds 1,236 dollars
lead.deck: Ten tenants attend at 10:04 a.m.; Mr. Ewald posts a letter to the company's box asking that the rent be called for; Mr. Raab's papers of July 15 still visible in it
lead.body: The ten tenants of the Vantry Arcade deposited the August rent of 412 dollars with Mr. Walter Ingersoll, clerk of the Municipal Court, at 10:04 a.m. yesterday, Mr. Nathan Ewald states, and the clerk now holds 1,236 dollars for Signal Ground Rents Inc. At 11:30 a.m. Mr. Ewald posted a letter to the company's post box in Long Island City asking that the rent be called for. The papers left in the box by Mr. Raab on July 15 remain visible through its window.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin reported over the Atlantic west of Spain; 'all well'
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin was over the Atlantic west of Spain at 4 p.m. yesterday, New York time, making about 70 miles an hour, the Navy states. Her message read 'All well.' Lady Grace Drummond-Hay's first dispatch was received at 6:12 p.m. and concerned breakfast.

columns.headline: Licence inspection reaches Ridgewood and Glendale; 3,622 licences granted
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors have visited 3,610 buildings since July 2, his office states, and moved to Ridgewood and Glendale this week. Licences granted number 3,622. Alderman John Feeney's application for the records of the 23 disputed primary districts will be heard on October 9.

columns.headline: Dr. Rastin applies in writing for the light company's Ruffle Bar note
columns.body: Dr. Emil Rastin of Columbia has written to Queens Light & Power asking for a copy of its observer's note of the four seconds without reading on Ruffle Bar on July 28, his office states. The company states that it has received the letter and that the note remains private.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, at Long Beach, Port Washington or Bay Shore.

speaker.ear: Warm. High 86. Friday. Eighteen Fridays. The Graf is halfway to us.

lead.headline: Pun Derby, week nine: the Zeppelin cards finally get off the ground
lead.deck: Two hundred airship entries held since July come down at last; an upholsterer from Glendale takes the five dollars; the horse's gasbag card ruled a horse pun after all
lead.body: Week nine goes to Mr. Otto Brandt, upholsterer, of Glendale, from the airship entries held since July: 'My husband is like the Zeppelin. Full of gas, and he only comes down when somebody pulls the line.' Mr. Brandt is not married. He says it came to him at the shop. Five dollars and a year's Speaker. Runner-up: a Corona girl whose brother talks so much the Navy has asked for his frequency. Mr. Kehoe's horse's gasbag card was ruled a horse pun.

columns.headline: Party Line's eighteenth Friday, and the parcel window stays switched off
columns.body: Eighteen Fridays. Party Line was at the parcel window at four, washed her face at a quarter past, and at five went back under the board. No tin from Corona. Sergeant Moran has given up carnivals and taken up the Woodside bowling green, for reasons he will not give.

columns.headline: The rent goes in, and Ewald drops the company a line
columns.body: Twelve hundred and thirty-six dollars now sit with the court clerk for Signal Ground Rents Inc., and yesterday Mr. Ewald wrote asking the company to come and get them. He posted it in its own box, on top of Mr. Raab's papers. Crowded, for a box nobody opens.

columns.headline: The Zeppelin's lady wires home about breakfast, and the Navy takes it down
columns.body: Lady Drummond-Hay's first message from the Graf reached Lakehurst at twelve minutes past six, from west of Spain. It was about breakfast: ham, rolls, coffee and a view. The Navy's operator took it down and asked for seconds. The ship says all is well, and she is making seventy.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The pool at the Arcade now says Ewald gets an answer before Raab does. Two to one. The cigar stand is holding the money.

lead.headline: Week's count: 1,688 night calls on the tone in Queens, the most recorded
lead.deck: Rise of 317 on the week, chiefly between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m.; operators' sheets describe the tone as 'nearer'; Brooklyn's door at 1,090; light company issues no statement
lead.body: The Queens Exchange logged 1,688 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting a tone, against 1,371, the most in any week since the count began, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states. More than half were placed between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m. Callers described the tone as 'nearer' and 'louder at night,' the operators' sheets show. The Brooklyn Exchange's door shows 1,090. Queens Light & Power issued no statement yesterday.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on an eighteenth Friday
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the eighteenth Friday without one, the supervisor states. The animal attended the parcel window from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. The warrant for Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman, remains outstanding.

columns.headline: Parks Department and Phonautograph Society open a children's recording contest
columns.body: Children of six to twelve may record one minute of 'anything that is theirs' at 20 playgrounds from Monday to August 14, the Parks Department states. The Phonautograph Society will judge. The prize is a fifteen-dollar home recorder, and the winning record goes into the Society's vault for 1978.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin 1,400 miles from Lakehurst at midnight; Navy stations sit today
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin was about 1,400 miles from Lakehurst at midnight, in mid-Atlantic against head winds, the Naval Air Station states. The Navy's seven receiving stations, from Lakehurst to Montauk Point, sit from 6 a.m. today. Her arrival is expected on Sunday evening.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 89. Saturday. Sixteen hundred calls. One hum. Louder.

lead.headline: The Hum turns up the volume after midnight, and Queens rings the operator
lead.deck: Sixteen hundred and eighty-eight calls in a week between one and four, the most ever; the operators' sheets say 'nearer'; the light company, asked for a word, does not give one
lead.body: This week Queens rang the operator sixteen hundred and eighty-eight times in the small hours to say that the tone was louder, and the operators, who could hear it too, wrote down 'nearer.' Most calls came between two and three. A Woodhaven grocer says it now comes up through his bed. A Maspeth mother says her baby hums along, in tune. The light company was asked for a statement yesterday and gave the usual one, which is none. Brooklyn's door is up to ten-ninety.

columns.headline: Children of Queens, step up to the record and say something for 1978
columns.body: From Monday, any child from six to twelve may record one minute of anything at twenty playgrounds, for the Phonautograph Society to judge. The prize is a home recorder. The winner goes in the vault for 1978. Mothers are asked not to coach. Fathers are asked not to enter.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike's three shores hold the line, and the Navy listens east
columns.body: Two weeks since Bay Shore and not a figure. Mr. Pike's men sit at Long Beach, Port Washington and Bay Shore, and from this morning the Navy's seven stations sit up for the Zeppelin. The office boy says that makes ten sets of ears. He wants it on the map.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: who will wear what to hear the Graf come in
columns.body: Darlings, the Listening Lady will be on the Lakehurst road on Sunday with half of Southampton. Mrs. Van Ness has a hat with a mooring mast on it. The Halloran girls are going by motor bus. Everyone is bringing a recorder for the engines, and nobody is bringing a sandwich.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Montauk Point, eleven tonight: the Navy's man says he hears 'a little something east.' The Navy says not yet.

editorial.headline: The market climbs and so do the warnings
editorial.body: The ticker's voice climbs a little higher every day this summer, and the Record prints its tone beside its figures, and the borough's widows have put their savings in Mr. Fenn's Trust at a guaranteed nine percent, the Speaker's own pension fund among them. This week leaflets appeared in every church porch in Queens, printed in purple ink, advising widows to take their money out of any trust that cannot show them the bonds it claims to hold. The leaflets are signed with a spider. This paper calls it scaremongering by a skirt. Nine percent is nine percent. We have asked Mr. Fenn to show us the bonds, purely to put the matter at rest. He is away.

lead.headline: Navy's Montauk station hears the Graf Zeppelin's engines at 1:12 a.m.
lead.deck: Ship's motors taken down 'faint and steady' some hours before any sighting; position about 300 miles east of Nantucket; landing at Lakehurst expected this evening
lead.body: The naval receiving station at Montauk Point took down the engines of the Graf Zeppelin at 1:12 a.m. today, 'faint and steady,' the Naval Air Station at Lakehurst states, the ship being then about 300 miles east of Nantucket by her own wire. No sighting is expected before noon. The landing at Lakehurst is set for this evening. The State Police will close the Lakehurst road to motor cars at 3 p.m. The ground crew of 350 reported at midnight.

columns.headline: Dr. Strand telegraphs the seminary a fourth time, from Bangor
columns.body: Union Seminary states that it received a telegram from Dr. Matthias Strand at 9:20 a.m. yesterday, sent from Bangor, Carnarvonshire. It read 'Still.' The seminary states that it has replied to the Bangor post office, the only address it holds, and that the chapel reopens in September.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society records Rockaway at low tide; 23 members attend
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens recorded the beach at Rockaway at low tide at dawn yesterday, Mr. Linus Fahey, secretary, states, 'the tide being a matter for 1978.' The record was kept with the tone. The Society will judge the children's contest at Borough Hall.

columns.headline: Stocks close the week at 359.4 at a short session; tone entered as 'level'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange closed the week at yesterday's short session on a volume of 1,980,000 shares, the industrial average standing at 359.4. The ticker was 3 minutes late at noon. Its tone was entered as 'level.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night by the Radio Division. The Navy has not stated what else Montauk heard.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 91. Sunday. You can hear her. You can't see her. Yet.

lead.headline: Montauk hears the Graf before anyone sees her, and the Island holds still
lead.deck: Twelve minutes past one, three hundred miles out, a hum on the Navy's set that is not the usual hum; the Lakehurst road shut to motors at three; bring a hat
lead.body: At twelve minutes past one this morning the Navy's man at Montauk Point heard engines out over the ocean, faint and steady, three hundred miles off, which is further than anyone in Montauk has ever heard anything. That was the Graf Zeppelin. Nobody will see her before noon. She comes down at Lakehurst this evening, and half of Long Island is going to watch. The State Police will shut the road at three. The other half will stay home and listen, which is cheaper.

columns.headline: Strand sends a fourth wire from Wales, and the seminary stays tuned
columns.body: 'Calm.' 'Nearly.' 'Here.' And yesterday, from Bangor again: 'Still.' That is Dr. Strand's fourth telegram to the seminary. Our man says it is a poem getting shorter. The seminary has written back to the Bangor post office. It is the only address they have.

columns.headline: The dog war: Bunny skips the Graf, and three owners hold their positions
columns.body: Rewards stand at two dollars for Bunny, five for Major and fifty cents for Pepper. Mrs. Ahl of Elmhurst says fifty cents is plenty for a dog who is hers anyway. Dr. Voight says he will be at Lakehurst tonight, in case. Nobody knows in case of what.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'What does a Zeppelin sound like?'
columns.body: Sir, according to the Navy man at Montauk, like five motor boats a long way off having an argument. According to Lady Drummond-Hay, like a very large sewing machine. The operator has not heard it. She has been working nights, and nights in Queens have their own sound.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Noon: sighted off Block Island, silver, enormous, and quieter than her own reputation.

lead.headline: Graf Zeppelin moored at Lakehurst at 7:42 p.m., 95 hours from Germany
lead.deck: About 20,000 on the field and the road; the crowd hears her engines 11 minutes before she clears the trees; Dr. Eckener's remarks recorded at the mast; world flight to begin on Wednesday night
lead.body: The Graf Zeppelin was made fast to the mast at the Naval Air Station at Lakehurst at 7:42 p.m. yesterday, about 95 hours from Friedrichshafen, the Navy states. About 20,000 persons lined the field and the road. Her engines were heard from the field 11 minutes before she cleared the pines. Dr. Hugo Eckener stated to the mast recorder that the crossing had been 'slow, against the wind.' The world flight will begin from Lakehurst on Wednesday night.

columns.headline: Navy's Montauk station logged WORS 1610 for six minutes on Saturday night
columns.body: The naval receiving station at Montauk Point, sitting for the Graf Zeppelin, logged figures on 1610 kilocycles for about six minutes from 2:02 a.m. Sunday, the Navy states. Mr. Harold Pike of the Radio Division has asked for the log and for a seat at Montauk.

columns.headline: Mr. Ruth hits his twenty-seventh home run; the Athletics lead by twelve
columns.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit his twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh home runs of the season over the week-end, the Yankees winning twice at the Stadium. The Athletics divided a double-header yesterday and lead the American League by twelve games. Brooklyn lost twice at Ebbets Field.

columns.headline: Heat rises for a fourth day: 93 at 3 p.m.; ice houses 'holding, with care'
columns.body: The temperature reached 93 degrees at 3 p.m. yesterday, the Weather Bureau states, and three persons were overcome in Queens. Mr. Gustave Pohl states that the ice companies' houses are 'holding, with care,' and that two further barges of Hudson ice are expected at Astoria on Wednesday.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night at any of the Radio Division's three places. Montauk did not state.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 93. Monday. She's down. She's tied up. Wednesday she goes round.

lead.headline: Lakehurst catches the Graf on the first ring, and twenty thousand hear her in
lead.deck: Eleven minutes of engines over the pines before anyone saw a thing; three hundred and fifty sailors get the line at last; Dr. Eckener says slow, and means the wind
lead.body: Twenty thousand people stood on the Lakehurst field last night and heard the Graf Zeppelin for eleven minutes before she showed over the pines, a long low drone that several ladies took for the Hum and several men for indigestion. Then there she was, silver, the size of a street. At eighteen minutes to eight the sailors got the line and walked her to the mast. Dr. Eckener told the recorder the crossing was slow. The passengers said it was lovely. On Wednesday she goes round the world.

columns.headline: WORS cuts in on the Zeppelin's party line, and the Navy takes six minutes down
columns.body: At two minutes past two on Sunday morning, while the Navy at Montauk sat up for the Graf, somebody else came on: six minutes of figures on sixteen-ten. The Navy logged it. Mr. Pike wants a chair at Montauk. Pin one hundred and two goes in.

columns.headline: The Babe connects twice more, and the Athletics still won't take his call
columns.body: Twenty-six and twenty-seven for the Babe over the week-end, two Yankee wins at the Stadium, and Philadelphia still twelve games up. Mr. Huggins says August is long. The Babe says five hundred is three away. Our sporting man is counting with him, on his fingers.

columns.headline: Ninety-three, and Mr. Pohl's ice houses put the borough on hold
columns.body: Ninety-three yesterday and three down in the street. Mr. Pohl says the ice houses are holding, with care, which means half a block to a cake and the rest Wednesday, when the barges come down the river. Nell the ice horse has a new hat, with a wider brim.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Dr. Voight, dentist, was at Lakehurst last night. He reports no terrier. He reports a very large airship.

record.ear: Hot. High 96. Low 77. Storms by evening, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Dr. Rastin finds the night tone a third stronger than in his June readings
lead.deck: Corona roof readings at 41 cycles show the tone rising after midnight and falling after 4 a.m.; Queens Exchange logs 288 calls on Sunday night; light company states 'nothing has changed on its system'
lead.body: Dr. Emil Rastin of Columbia states that his readings from a roof in Corona since July 30 show the tone at 41 cycles about one third stronger between midnight and 4 a.m. than in his June readings, and no stronger by day. The Queens Exchange logged 288 calls reporting the tone between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. on Sunday night. Queens Light & Power states that 'nothing has changed on its system' and that it has not received Dr. Rastin's figures.

columns.headline: Fifth day of heat: 94 at 3:10 p.m.; four overcome; 5,600 in the playgrounds
columns.body: The temperature reached 94 degrees at 3:10 p.m. yesterday, the Weather Bureau states, and four persons were overcome in Queens. About 5,600 slept in the playgrounds. The Bureau forecasts thunderstorms late today and cooler weather tomorrow. Ice stands at 55 cents the hundredweight.

columns.headline: Children's recording contest: 1,140 entries taken on the first day
columns.body: The Parks Department states that 1,140 children recorded entries at 20 playgrounds yesterday, the first day of the children's recording contest, the queue at Juniper Valley reaching 300 at noon. Most entries are songs. Eleven are of dogs. One, from Astoria, is of a fire.

columns.headline: Reparations conference opens at The Hague today; hall fitted with recorders
columns.body: The conference of the powers on the Young plan for German reparations opens at The Hague today, the State Department states. The Dutch Government has fitted the hall of the Binnenhof with recorders 'for the delegations' use only.' Mr. Philip Snowden heads the British delegation.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Pike sat at Montauk last night, his fourth place, the Radio Division states. WORS 1610 was not heard.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 96. Tuesday. Storms tonight. The Hum won't notice.

lead.headline: Rastin's meter says the Hum turns it up a third when the lights go out
lead.deck: Forty-one cycles, same as ever, only bigger after midnight and back to normal by four; the light company says nothing's changed, and hasn't read the figures to know
lead.body: Dr. Rastin has been on a Corona roof every night for a week with his meter, and says the tone is the same tone, forty-one cycles, only a third bigger between midnight and four than it was in June. By day, no change. The light company says nothing has changed on its system and that it has not seen Dr. Rastin's figures, which is one way of making sure. Two hundred and eighty-eight Queens households rang the operator about it on Sunday night. The operator said yes.

columns.headline: Eleven dogs and a fire: the children's contest takes its first thousand calls
columns.body: Eleven hundred and forty children recorded a minute each yesterday, the contest's first day. Most sang. Eleven recorded their dogs. One Astoria boy recorded his own account of the Ditmars fire, with sirens, which he did with his mouth. The Society's judges are said to be bracing themselves.

columns.headline: The Hague hears reparations, and the Dutch keep the records on a short wire
columns.body: The powers meet at The Hague today about what Germany owes and when, and the Dutch have wired the hall for sound, for the delegates only. Mr. Snowden of Britain says he will not budge an inch. The recorders will have that on file by teatime.

columns.headline: Ninety-four, and the Weather Bureau promises a thunderous reception
columns.body: Ninety-four at ten past three yesterday, four down, fifty-six hundred in the schoolyards, and the Bureau promises thunderstorms tonight and something cooler tomorrow. The Bureau has promised before. Mr. Pohl's barges are due at Astoria tomorrow, which is a promise you can put butter on.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Thunder over Flushing at a quarter to five. It is raining on the Arcade. The cigar stand has put the papers inside.

lead.headline: Thunderstorm ends six days of heat; temperature falls 24 degrees in 90 minutes
lead.deck: 96 at 3 p.m., 72 at 4:30 p.m.; lightning strikes the Woodside gas holder without damage; Queens Exchange logs no tone calls during the storm and 312 after 1 a.m.
lead.body: A thunderstorm ended six days of heat yesterday, the temperature falling from 96 degrees at 3 p.m. to 72 at 4:30 p.m., the Weather Bureau states. About 1.4 inches of rain fell at Jamaica. Lightning struck the gas holder at Woodside at 4:12 p.m. without damage. Cellars flooded in Corona and Maspeth. The Queens Exchange logged no calls reporting the tone during the storm, and 312 between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. today.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its twentieth week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its twentieth week. Senator Rufus Keel has written again, asking only whether the record is 'still there.' It is.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin to leave Lakehurst tonight on her flight round the world
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin will leave the mast at Lakehurst tonight on her flight round the world by way of Friedrichshafen, Tokyo and Los Angeles, the Navy states. Each passenger's voice is to be recorded on boarding. This newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue will play her messages as received.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Circle of Flushing meets tonight to hear its second record
columns.body: The Phonautograph Circle of Flushing meets at 8 p.m. tonight at the Flushing Free Library to hear its second record, of the Flushing Meadow dumps at night, made with the tone removed, Mr. Irving Moss, president, states. Mrs. Ottoline Grieve has given notice of a motion.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, at any of its four places.

speaker.ear: Cool at last. High 79. Wednesday. The Graf goes round tonight.

lead.headline: The storm clears the static, and Queens drops twenty-four degrees in a crash
lead.deck: Ninety-six at three, seventy-two at half past four; the Woodside gas holder takes a bolt and shrugs; nobody rings about the Hum till one in the morning
lead.body: At three o'clock yesterday it was ninety-six and Queens was cooking. At half past four it was seventy-two and Queens was wet. In between came the loudest ninety minutes of the summer. Lightning hit the Woodside gas holder at twelve past four, and the gas holder, to everyone's relief, did nothing. Corona's cellars filled. Children ran in the gutters. The operators say nobody rang about the night tone while the thunder lasted, and at one o'clock they started again.

columns.headline: The Graf goes round the world tonight, and every passenger signs in by voice
columns.body: At the Lakehurst mast tonight each passenger says a word into the Navy's machine and climbs aboard for Friedrichshafen, Tokyo, Los Angeles and home. The Record's window on Jackson Avenue will play her wires as they come in. We will print them as they go out.

columns.headline: The Senate's 'resent' reaches week twenty, and Keel calls back
columns.body: Twenty weeks in the Albany vault, and the one word on the Senate's March record is unclaimed. Last week Senator Keel did not write and Mr. Pratt noticed. This week the Senator wrote to ask if it was still there. It is. Mr. Pratt was seen smiling.

columns.headline: Flushing's Circle meets tonight, and Mrs. Grieve wants the tone back on
columns.body: Mr. Moss's Circle meets at the library tonight to play its second tone-free record, the Flushing dumps by night. Mrs. Grieve has given notice of a motion. The motion is that the Circle record with the tone left in. Mr. Abbot is still not invited.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Lakehurst, nine o'clock: passengers at the mast, Lady Drummond-Hay recorded saying 'Ready,' and the sailors on the line.

lead.headline: Graf Zeppelin leaves Lakehurst at 11:40 p.m. on her flight round the world
lead.deck: 18 passengers' voices recorded at the mast; the ship's engines heard at Montauk from 2:31 a.m. to 3:50 a.m.; her first message played in this newspaper's window at 1:15 a.m.
lead.body: The Graf Zeppelin left the mast at Lakehurst at 11:40 p.m. yesterday on her flight round the world, the Navy states, with 18 passengers under Dr. Hugo Eckener. The naval station at Montauk Point heard her engines from 2:31 a.m. until 3:50 a.m. Her first message was played in this newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue at 1:15 a.m. to about 200 persons. It read 'Course east, all well.'

columns.headline: Phonautograph Circle votes nine to eight against recording with the tone
columns.body: The Phonautograph Circle of Flushing heard its second record, of the Flushing Meadow dumps at night, at the library last night, Mr. Irving Moss states. Mrs. Ottoline Grieve moved that the Circle record with the tone left in. The motion was lost, nine votes to eight.

columns.headline: Licence inspectors to inspect one another's houses, Mr. Crane orders
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane has ordered that the 62 inspectors of his office be inspected at their own residences, his office states, after a Ridgewood landlord asked to see the licence of the inspector at his door. Inspectors will inspect in pairs, neither in his own district.

columns.headline: Mr. Crane rules the Ditmars Avenue seal stays until the owner is found
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane has ruled under section 9 that the seal on the Ditmars Avenue room is to remain until the owner of the house is found, his office states, refusing the Signal Exchange's application. The Exchange will advertise for the owner. The room's system has not been reconnected.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night at the Radio Division's four places, the Division states.

speaker.ear: Cool. High 80. Thursday. The Graf's gone round the corner.

lead.headline: The Graf hangs up on Lakehurst and puts the whole world on hold
lead.deck: Twenty to midnight, eighteen passengers say a word each into the mast machine and the ship goes east; Montauk hears her for an hour and twenty minutes, then nothing but sea
lead.body: At twenty minutes to midnight the sailors let go the line and the Graf Zeppelin went up off Lakehurst for Friedrichshafen, Tokyo, Los Angeles and back, the long way round. Each of the eighteen passengers said one word into the mast machine before boarding. Lady Drummond-Hay said 'Ready.' Sir Hubert Wilkins said 'Cheerio.' Mr. von Wiegand said 'Copy.' The Navy's Montauk man heard her engines until ten to four, and after that only the Atlantic. She will ring when she gets there.

columns.headline: Crane's inspectors turn the switch on themselves, and Ridgewood listens in
columns.body: A Ridgewood landlord asked the inspector at his door to show his own licence, and he had none. Mr. Crane has now ordered all sixty-two of his men to inspect each other, in pairs. It is the first inspection in Queens that everybody wants to attend.

columns.headline: The Circle votes nine to eight to keep the Hum off the record
columns.body: Mrs. Grieve's motion to put the tone back into the Flushing Circle's records lost by one vote last night. Mr. Moss voted with the nine. Mrs. Grieve sat very still. The second record, of the Flushing dumps by night, was described as 'smaller again.'

columns.headline: The Ditmars seal stays on, and the room keeps its own counsel
columns.body: Mr. Crane has ruled that the sealed room on Ditmars Avenue stays sealed until somebody can find who owns the house. The Exchange will advertise. The room heard the fire three minutes before anybody else did. Nobody has asked it what else it heard.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Record's window at a quarter past one this morning: two hundred in the street in nightclothes, hearing 'Course east, all well.' Then they went to bed.

lead.headline: Reserve Bank of New York raises its rediscount rate to 6 per cent
lead.deck: Directors' decision given out at 4:40 p.m., after the close; the day's volume 3,780,000 shares, industrial average 356.2; tone book's 3 p.m. entry 'held'; brokers' wires in Queens open past 8 p.m.
lead.body: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York raised its rediscount rate from 5 to 6 per cent yesterday, the decision being given out at 4:40 p.m., after the close of the Stock Exchange, the bank states. Prices had eased during the day on a volume of 3,780,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 356.2. The tone book records the ticker's tone at 3 p.m. as 'held.' Brokers' offices in Jamaica and Flushing kept their wires open past 8 p.m. answering inquiries.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin reported 1,100 miles east of Montauk; liner hears her engines
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin was about 1,100 miles east of Montauk Point at 6 p.m. yesterday, by her own wire, making 80 miles an hour with a following wind. The North German Lloyd liner Bremen reports that its receiving room heard her engines for 40 minutes at about noon.

columns.headline: Children's recording contest closes its first week with 4,310 entries
columns.body: The Parks Department states that 4,310 children had recorded entries in the children's recording contest by last night. The Phonautograph Society's judges have begun to hear them at Borough Hall, eight hours a day. Entries close at 6 p.m. on Wednesday.

columns.headline: Light company answers Dr. Rastin's letter; note 'remains the company's'
columns.body: Queens Light & Power has replied to Dr. Emil Rastin's letter of August 1 asking for its observer's note of the four seconds on Ruffle Bar, his office states. The reply, of one paragraph, states that the note 'remains the company's.' Dr. Rastin will continue his night readings in Corona.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 82. Friday. Nineteen Fridays. Six per cent. Hold on.

lead.headline: The Reserve rings up six per cent, and Wall Street's line goes very quiet
lead.deck: The bank waits till the ticker stops and then raises the rate a whole point; Jamaica's brokers answer the telephone till eight; the tone book says 'held,' and so is everybody's breath
lead.body: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York waited yesterday until the ticker had stopped for the day, then put its rate up from five to six per cent, which is the bank's way of saying calm down. The ticker had spent the afternoon sounding 'held,' says the tone book, which is how you sound when you know something is coming. Brokers in Jamaica and Flushing answered telephones until eight. Most callers asked one question. The brokers gave one answer: hold on.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week ten: a switchman holds the line, and the Speaker pays five
columns.body: Week ten goes to Mr. Lou Abend, retired switchman, of Kew Gardens: 'A broker is like an operator. He says hold the line, and you do, and he doesn't.' Five dollars and a year's Speaker. He has held both, and prefers the line.

columns.headline: Party Line's nineteenth Friday, and nobody rings the parcel bell
columns.body: Nineteen Fridays. Party Line at the window at four, nose to the grille. At five she went back under the board. No tin from Corona. Sergeant Moran's bowling green turns out to be next door to a linemen's lodge. He says it is a coincidence.

columns.headline: Rastin writes, and the light company answers in the usual key
columns.body: Dr. Rastin wrote to the light company for its man's note of the four quiet seconds on Ruffle Bar. The company wrote back a paragraph saying the note is the company's. Its first answer to anybody in writing. It said nothing, but on paper.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Ewald's letter to the company is still in its box at six o'clock, on top of Mr. Raab's papers. The pool has lengthened the odds.

lead.headline: Stocks fall on 5,600,000 shares after the rate rise; ticker 38 minutes late
lead.deck: Industrial average down 12.4 to 343.8, the month's lowest; tone book enters 'dropped, hollow' at 10:20 a.m. and 'steadying' at 2:50 p.m.; Queens brokers call 212 margin accounts by operator
lead.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange fell yesterday on a volume of 5,600,000 shares, the largest of the summer, following the Reserve Bank's rise in its rate, the industrial average closing at 343.8, a loss of 12.4. The ticker ran 38 minutes late. The tone book records the tone at 10:20 a.m. as 'dropped, hollow' and at 2:50 p.m. as 'steadying.' Brokers in Queens placed about 212 calls for further margin through the operators, the Queens Exchange states.

columns.headline: Week's count: 2,214 night calls on the tone; 1,233 on the Brooklyn door
columns.body: The Queens Exchange logged 2,214 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting a tone, against 1,688, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, the greater part between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m. The Brooklyn Exchange's door shows 1,233.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on a nineteenth Friday
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the nineteenth Friday without one, the supervisor states. The animal attended the parcel window from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. The warrant for Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman, remains outstanding.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin crosses the French coast; due at Friedrichshafen today
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin crossed the coast of France near Bordeaux at 9:20 p.m. yesterday, New York time, the Berlin wire states, and is expected at Friedrichshafen this morning, their time. Her messages are being played in this newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue as received.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 83. Saturday. Wall Street fell over. Then it got up.

lead.headline: Wall Street drops the receiver, and the margin calls come through Queens
lead.deck: Thirty-eight minutes of ticker behind, twelve points off the average and two hundred and twelve brokers asking the operator for a client who had gone out to lunch
lead.body: Yesterday at twenty past ten the tone book wrote down 'dropped, hollow,' which is how the ticker sounded when the rate rise hit it, and the industrials went down twelve points like a man missing a stair. Then the Queens operators had a morning. Two hundred and twelve brokers rang clients for more margin, most of whom had gone to lunch, and some of whom have gone to Atlantic City. By ten to three the tone book said 'steadying.' Our financial editor said the same, twice.

columns.headline: Twenty-two hundred calls, and the Hum is the busiest subscriber in Queens
columns.body: Two thousand two hundred and fourteen calls this week about the night tone, up five hundred, most of them between two and three. Superintendent Arne has put four more girls on the small hours. Brooklyn's door says twelve-thirty-three. Mr. Tully of Brooklyn says Queens is copying.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike takes a chair at Montauk, and sits on it
columns.body: Mr. Pike now keeps four sets of men: Long Beach, Port Washington, Bay Shore and Montauk Point, where the Navy heard six minutes last Sunday. Five nights at Montauk, nothing. The office boy says WORS was following the Zeppelin and has gone to Germany.

columns.headline: The Graf rings in from Bordeaux, and Jackson Avenue stays up to answer
columns.body: The Graf crossed into France near Bordeaux last night, and the Record's window on Jackson Avenue played her wire to a crowd of a hundred and forty, including two policemen and a milkman. She lands at Friedrichshafen this morning. The milkman says she is late.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Friedrichshafen, eight this morning their time: down, fast and home. Fifty-five hours from Lakehurst. Somebody tell the milkman.

editorial.headline: A woman cannot fly, and Lilith proves it again
editorial.body: The Graf Zeppelin is to fly round the world, and the women of America will be told about it by their husbands. That is the natural order and the Speaker defends it. A woman cannot fly; Lilith proved it again on Thursday by gliding, on a cape of black silk, from the roof of the Fenn Building to the roof of the borough bank across the plaza, a distance our engineer puts at ninety feet, which is not flying, merely falling with an aim. She carried with her the bank's own record of the Fenn Trust's deposits, which she left with the bank examiner. Miss Earhart, who also cannot fly, is entered in a race across the country.

lead.headline: Graf Zeppelin lands at Friedrichshafen 55 hours out of Lakehurst
lead.deck: The Atlantic crossed eastward in the shortest time on record; the landing heard in this newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue by about 90 persons; ship to leave for Tokyo on Thursday
lead.body: The Graf Zeppelin landed at Friedrichshafen at 8:24 a.m. yesterday, their time, or 2:24 a.m. by New York time, about 55 hours from Lakehurst, the Berlin wire states, the fastest crossing of the Atlantic eastward. The wire's record of the landing, the ground crew's cheering included, was played in this newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue at 2:31 a.m. to about 90 persons. The ship will leave for Tokyo on Thursday, by way of Siberia.

columns.headline: Stocks recover part of Friday's loss at a short session; tone 'mending'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange recovered part of Friday's loss at yesterday's short session, on a volume of 2,750,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 349.1, a gain of 5.3. The ticker was 9 minutes late at noon. Its tone was entered as 'mending.'

columns.headline: Second postcard from Dr. Strand shows the same chapel and bears no message
columns.body: Union Seminary states that it received a second postcard from Dr. Matthias Strand yesterday, posted at Bangor on August 1 and showing the same chapel as the first. The reverse bears the address and nothing else. The seminary has not identified the chapel.

columns.headline: Society's judges have heard 1,880 of 5,460 children's entries
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society's judges had heard 1,880 of the children's recording contest's 5,460 entries at Borough Hall by last night, Mr. Linus Fahey, secretary, states. The judges sit eight hours a day and have asked the Parks Department for a second reproducer.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, at any of its four places.

speaker.ear: Warm. High 84. Sunday. One dog, three owners, one record.

lead.headline: The dog war goes on the record, and three owners claim the same bark
lead.deck: A Sunnyside girl of eight enters the children's contest with a minute of a wire-haired terrier who turned up at her back step; Woodside, Jackson Heights and Elmhurst each say that's my dog
lead.body: Little Ruthie Danko, eight, of Sunnyside, entered the children's recording contest on Thursday with one minute of a terrier who has been eating at her back step since Tuesday. Brown ear. Belled collar. Barks, the judges say, at about A. Within a day Mrs. Fitch, Dr. Voight and Mrs. Ahl had all heard of it and all asked to hear the record. The Society says entries are private until judging. The terrier has since left Ruthie's step. Ruthie says he will be back Tuesday.

columns.headline: Strand's second postcard: same chapel, same dead air on the back
columns.body: Dr. Strand's second postcard reached the seminary yesterday: the same chapel as the first, posted at Bangor on the first of August, and on the back the address and nothing else. Our Chester cousin says if it is the same chapel, he is at least staying put.

columns.headline: The Graf lands in Germany, and Jackson Avenue picks up the cheering
columns.body: Fifty-five hours from Lakehurst to Friedrichshafen, the fastest ever eastward, and at half past two yesterday morning ninety people on Jackson Avenue, in nightshirts, heard the German ground crew cheer through the Record's window. Some of them cheered back. The Germans did not hear.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Is the Babe going to hit five hundred?'
columns.body: Sir, the operator does not take bets, but she notes that Mr. Ruth has four hundred and ninety-nine and is in Cleveland today. If he does, the Record's window will play it, and the operator expects a great many calls from people asking whether he did.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The terrier was seen at four o'clock outside the Sunnyside library, listening to the band. All three owners are on the way.

lead.headline: Mr. Ruth hits his 500th home run at Cleveland; Yankees lose by 6 to 5
lead.deck: Ball cleared the right-field wall at League Park in the second inning off Mr. Willis Hudlin; the wire's record of the hit played in this newspaper's window at 2:31 p.m. to about 1,500 persons
lead.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit the five hundredth home run of his career, and his thirtieth of the season, at League Park, Cleveland, yesterday, in the second inning off Mr. Willis Hudlin, the ball clearing the right-field wall. The Yankees lost by 6 to 5. The wire's record of the hit, the crowd included, was played in this newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue at 2:31 p.m. to about 1,500 persons. The man who caught the ball returned it for 20 dollars.

columns.headline: The Athletics win twice and lead the American League by thirteen games
columns.body: The Athletics won twice yesterday and lead the American League by thirteen games over the Yankees, who lost at Cleveland. Brooklyn divided a double-header at Ebbets Field before about 31,000. The Giants lost at the Polo Grounds.

columns.headline: Children's recording contest entries reach 6,240; winner to be named Thursday
columns.body: The Parks Department states that 6,240 entries had been recorded in the children's recording contest by Saturday night, and that entries close at 6 p.m. on Wednesday. The Phonautograph Society's judges at Borough Hall expect to name the winner on Thursday afternoon.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin to take on gas at Friedrichshafen; departs for Tokyo Thursday
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin will take on fuel gas and stores at Friedrichshafen until Wednesday and leave for Tokyo early on Thursday, their time, by way of Berlin and Siberia, the Zeppelin company states by the Berlin wire. Dr. Hugo Eckener will command.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Warm. High 86. Monday. Five hundred. Say it twice.

lead.headline: The Babe rings up number five hundred, and Jackson Avenue answers
lead.deck: Second inning at Cleveland, Mr. Hudlin's pitch over the right-field wall and into the street; fifteen hundred in Queens hear it on the Record's wire at half past two, and the Yankees still lose
lead.body: Babe Ruth hit his five hundredth home run yesterday in Cleveland, the first man ever to get there, and at half past two fifteen hundred people on Jackson Avenue heard it, crack and roar and all, through the Record's window. They cheered. A man in a straw hat wept. The ball went over the right-field wall into the street, and the fellow who caught it gave it back for twenty dollars and another ball. The Yankees lost, six to five. Nobody on Jackson Avenue cared.

columns.headline: Philadelphia goes thirteen up, and the pennant is on the line
columns.body: The Athletics won two yesterday and are thirteen games clear with seven weeks to play. Brooklyn split, the Giants lost, and Mr. Huggins said nothing at Cleveland, which our sporting man says is a first. The Babe, asked about the pennant, talked about the ball.

columns.headline: Six thousand children on the record, and the judges ask for earmuffs
columns.body: Sixty-two hundred children have recorded a minute each, the contest closes Wednesday, and the Society's judges at Borough Hall are hearing them eight hours a day. One judge has asked to be excused from dogs. Another from the Sidewalks of New York, which has been sung four hundred times.

columns.headline: The dog war: the terrier misses the library band, and three owners miss him
columns.body: All three owners reached the Sunnyside library at a quarter past four yesterday. The terrier had gone at ten past. They stood together on the steps for some time. Mrs. Ahl offered the others a peppermint. Both refused. Rewards stand at two dollars, five and fifty cents.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Babe's record is to be played again in the Record's window at noon today, by request of three hundred letters and one priest.

lead.headline: 14 of Mr. Crane's 62 licence inspectors found to have unlicensed systems
lead.deck: Inspection of the inspectors completed in five days; one inspector's system 'installed in 1909 and never applied for'; the fourteen given 30 days and continuing to inspect
lead.body: Fourteen of the 62 licence inspectors of Mr. Hollis Crane's office were found to have unlicensed listening systems in their own residences, the office states, the inspection of the inspectors having been completed in five days. One system had been 'installed in 1909 and never applied for.' The fourteen have been given 30 days to apply and will continue to inspect in the meantime. The Ridgewood landlord whose question began the inspection has been licensed.

columns.headline: Mr. Ewald's letter and Mr. Raab's papers remain in the company's box
columns.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald's letter of August 1 to Signal Ground Rents Inc. remained in the company's post box at Long Island City at 5 p.m. yesterday, with the papers left by Mr. Raab on July 15, the post office states. The court clerk holds 1,236 dollars.

columns.headline: Night tone two fifths stronger than in June, Dr. Rastin's figures show
columns.body: Dr. Emil Rastin's readings in Corona for the week to Sunday show the tone at 41 cycles about two fifths stronger between midnight and 4 a.m. than in June. Queens Light & Power states that it 'does not comment on Dr. Rastin's figures.'

columns.headline: Board of Elections' counting room licensed; the 23 records not applied for
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's office granted the Board of Elections a licence for the system in its counting room at Long Island City yesterday, his office states. Chairman Delaney states that the Board has not applied, and will not apply, for the records of the 23 disputed primary districts.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 85. Tuesday. Fourteen inspectors. Thirty days. Nobody laughing.

lead.headline: Crane's men inspect each other, and fourteen are caught with their wires down
lead.deck: One in four of the borough's licence inspectors has an unlicensed system at home; one installed in 1909 and never mentioned; the fourteen have thirty days and keep their badges meanwhile
lead.body: Last week Mr. Crane's sixty-two licence inspectors were sent to inspect each other, and this week the results are in: fourteen of them have unlicensed listening systems at home. One had a system put in before the war and had simply never mentioned it, including to himself. The fourteen have thirty days to apply, and in the meantime will go on knocking on your door to ask about yours. The Ridgewood landlord who started it all has his licence now. He has had it framed.

columns.headline: Delaney licenses the room, and leaves the twenty-three records on hold
columns.body: The Board of Elections got its counting-room licence from Mr. Crane yesterday. Chairman Delaney says, again, that the Board will not ask for the twenty-three disputed records in Mr. Crane's vault. Alderman Feeney has asked, and will be heard in October. He is practising.

columns.headline: The Hum goes up two fifths after midnight, and the light company goes deaf
columns.body: Dr. Rastin says the night tone is now two fifths louder than in June, the same forty-one cycles, after midnight only. The light company now says it does not comment on his figures. It used to deny them. A Woodside man has moved his bed to the kitchen.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Has the company answered Mr. Ewald?'
columns.body: Sir, Signal Ground Rents Inc. has no telephone, so the operator would be the last to know. As of five o'clock, Mr. Ewald's letter was still in the company's box, on top of Mr. Raab's papers. The operator would also like her letters answered. She has written to the Hum.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The children's contest closes tomorrow at six. Queue at the Juniper Valley playground this afternoon: four hundred, and a goat.

lead.headline: Children's recording contest closes tonight with about 7,000 entries
lead.deck: Judges to name the winner tomorrow at 3 p.m.; most entries songs, 214 of dogs, 61 of grandparents speaking other languages; the winning record to be placed in the Phonautograph Society's vault
lead.body: The children's recording contest of the Parks Department closes at 6 p.m. today with about 7,000 entries from 20 playgrounds, Commissioner Ambrose Tuttle states. The Phonautograph Society's judges will name the winner at Borough Hall at 3 p.m. tomorrow. Mr. Linus Fahey, secretary, states that most entries are songs, that 214 are of dogs, and that 61 are of grandparents speaking languages other than English. The winning record will be placed in the Society's vault for 1978.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its twenty-first week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its twenty-first week. Senator Rufus Keel has written to ask 'who else asks.' Mr. Pratt states that nobody else asks.

columns.headline: Mr. Gorman asks again for the court's calendar of September 23
columns.body: Mr. Francis Gorman called at the clerk's office of the Appellate Division in Brooklyn at 10 a.m. yesterday and asked again for the calendar for September 23, the clerk states. None has been printed. Mr. Gorman stated that it was 'forty-one days' and left.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin to leave Friedrichshafen for Tokyo tonight, New York time
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin will leave Friedrichshafen for Tokyo at about 4:30 a.m. tomorrow, their time, or 10:30 p.m. tonight by New York time, with 20 passengers. The flight of about 6,800 miles crosses Siberia. This newspaper's window will play her messages as received.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, at any of its four places.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 84. Wednesday. The contest closes at six. Bring the dog.

lead.headline: Seven thousand kids get a minute on the record, and the judges go hoarse
lead.deck: Two hundred and fourteen dogs, sixty-one grandmothers in other languages, four hundred Sidewalks of New York and one boy from Long Island City who recorded a minute of nothing
lead.body: The children's recording contest closes at six tonight with about seven thousand entries, and the Phonautograph Society's judges, who have been listening eight hours a day at Borough Hall, will name the winner tomorrow. They have heard two hundred and fourteen dogs, sixty-one grandmothers, a goat, a fire, a canary that knows a little Verdi, and the Sidewalks of New York four hundred times. One Long Island City boy recorded a minute of his street at three in the morning. The judges played it twice.

columns.headline: The Graf takes off for Tokyo tonight, and the Record's window stays up late
columns.body: Tonight at half past ten our time the Graf leaves Friedrichshafen for Tokyo, sixty-eight hundred miles, most of it Siberia, where nobody has a receiving set. The Record's window will play whatever comes through. Our office boy is taking a blanket and a sandwich.

columns.headline: Gorman asks for September again, and the clerk gives him a busy signal
columns.body: Mr. Gorman was back at the Appellate Division clerk's window yesterday at ten, asking for the calendar of the twenty-third of September. Not printed. He said 'forty-one days' and went. We counted. He is right. He has been right every time.

columns.headline: Week twenty-one: Keel asks who else is calling about 'resent'
columns.body: Twenty-one weeks in the vault at Albany. This week Senator Keel wrote to ask the clerk who else asks about the March record. Mr. Pratt wrote back that nobody else asks. The Speaker would like it known that we ask, every week, and so does the Senator.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Long Island City, ten past five: Mr. Ewald's afternoon post brings a typed envelope from the company's box number. Inside, one word. Tomorrow.

lead.headline: Signal Ground Rents answers Mr. Ewald's letter in one word: 'Held'
lead.deck: Typed reply from the company's box number reaches the Arcade by the afternoon post; unsigned; postmarked Long Island City, August 13, 6 p.m.; Mr. Raab's papers and Mr. Ewald's letter gone from the box
lead.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald, for the tenants of the Vantry Arcade, received by the afternoon post yesterday a reply from the post box of Signal Ground Rents Inc. to his letter of August 1 asking the company to call for its rent. It is the company's first reply to any letter. The envelope is typed and postmarked Long Island City, August 13, 6 p.m. The reply, unsigned, is one word: 'Held.' The post office states that the box was emptied on Tuesday. The court clerk holds 1,236 dollars.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin leaves Friedrichshafen for Tokyo at 10:35 p.m., New York time
columns.body: The Graf Zeppelin left Friedrichshafen for Tokyo at 4:35 a.m. today, their time, or 10:35 p.m. yesterday by New York time, the Berlin wire states, with 20 passengers. Her course is by way of Berlin and Siberia. Her first message read 'Course east-northeast.'

columns.headline: Children's recording contest closes with 7,112 entries; winner named today
columns.body: The children's recording contest closed at 6 p.m. yesterday with 7,112 entries, the Parks Department states. The Phonautograph Society's judges will name the winner at Borough Hall at 3 p.m. today. The record of a Long Island City boy's street at night has been 'set aside.'

columns.headline: Stocks rise on 3,950,000 shares; tone book enters 'bright again'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 3,950,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 354.7, a gain of 2.9. The ticker ran 11 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'bright again.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 82. Thursday. The company spoke. One word. Read on.

lead.headline: The company finally picks up, says one word, and hangs up
lead.deck: After two months of no telephone, no answer and no collector, Signal Ground Rents writes back to the Arcade: 'Held.' Typed, unsigned, postmarked Tuesday at six; the box empty at last
lead.body: Since June, when the company took the Arcade's ground rent, the tenants have rung, written, knocked, sued and paid into court, and Signal Ground Rents Inc. has said nothing. Yesterday Mr. Ewald's post brought a typed envelope from the company's box number, and inside it, in answer to his letter about the twelve hundred and thirty-six dollars, one word: 'Held.' No signature. The box is empty now, Mr. Raab's papers with it. The Arcade pool has paid out. Nobody at the Arcade feels like they won.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'What does Held mean?'
columns.body: Madam, the operator says 'please hold' forty times an hour and has never been asked what it means. It means wait. It does not say for how long. The operator suggests you ask the company, but the company has said its word, and does not appear to have another.

columns.headline: The Graf goes east for Tokyo, and the office boy goes home with his blanket
columns.body: The Graf left Friedrichshafen at twenty-five to eleven last night our time, bound for Tokyo over Siberia. Her first wire said course east-northeast, which our office boy heard in the Record's window in his blanket. Then he went home, because Siberia will take a while.

columns.headline: The dog war: the terrier keeps his Tuesday date, then cuts the connection
columns.body: The terrier was back on Ruthie Danko's Sunnyside step on Tuesday, as she said he would be, and ate a sausage and left before anybody could ring Woodside, Jackson Heights or Elmhurst. The contest winner is named today. Ruthie's entry is the dog. She would like the recorder.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Borough Hall, three o'clock: the contest goes to a Ridgewood girl of nine, for a minute of her grandmother singing in Hungarian. The vault for 1978 has its first lullaby.
